## Draft Proposal - Subject to Review

This document is a **draft proposal** developed by the **CSI Team (Cloud Services Infrastructure)**. It is a navigational index, not an authorization artifact, control-inheritance claim, or assessment result, and has not been reviewed or approved by the {{< meta agency.short >}} CIO Office, the Office of Information Security (OIS), or organizational leadership.

**Date Code:** 2026-07-14 10:17 ET
:::

# Purpose

This appendix is the **series-wide control crosswalk** for the Federal
Application-Aware Networking (AAN) program. It answers one question directly:
*for a given NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control, where in the ten-volume series is it
addressed?* Use it as a reverse index when responding to an assessor, building a
System Security Plan control-origination table, or checking that a control family
is covered before an authorization review.

Across the 149 distinct controls indexed here, the series addresses coverage
spanning Volumes I through IX — the transport, data-platform, security-operations,
governance, training, and implementation layers, plus the three coordination and
day-2 volumes: **Volume VII (ServiceNow control-compliance automation)**,
**Volume VIII (multi-cloud DDI landing-zone automation)**, and **Volume IX
(ServiceNow day-2 operations)**. Those three do not, in the main, close *new*
control numbers — they *coordinate, evidence, and operate* controls the
architecture volumes already close, routing drift to owners and reconciling every
asset to the CM-8 join key (the genuinely new control numbers they add are
**CM-5** (separation-of-duties over DDI change) plus AC-2(3), AC-2(4), and SA-9(2) from Vol IX Book 05).

::: {.aan-warning}
## Maintenance status — a machine-derived slice now exists; this master table remains the hand-maintained superset

The **per-book "Authorities Closed Here" tables are generated** from
`aan-compliance-spine.yml` by `render_authorities_table.py`, and a CI drift gate
(`--check`, `.github/workflows/aan-authorities-drift.yml`) blocks any partial
that diverges from the spine. A **spine-derived crosswalk is now generated too**
— `render_crosswalk.py` renders [`AAN_Spine_Crosswalk.md`](AAN_Spine_Crosswalk.md)
from the same closures and is behind the same drift gate, so the machine-derived
slice can never silently fall out of sync with the spine. That slice currently
covers the **91 closures across 17 of 67 books** the spine carries (53 distinct
controls). **This series-wide master table below is still the hand-maintained
superset** — it indexes all 149 controls, including the books the spine has not
yet back-filled — so treat it as an author-maintained index, and read the
generated slice for the machine-verified subset. As the spine is back-filled book
by book, the generated slice grows toward this master automatically.
:::

# How This Crosswalk Was Built

The mapping is **extracted from each book's own primary control treatment** — the
"NIST 800-53 Rev 5 Control Closure" / "Authorities Closed Here" tables and the
sections where a control is the substantive subject. Controls that a book only
mentions in passing, cites in a framework-alignment cross-reference, or names in a
vendor appendix are deliberately **excluded**, so a row here means the series
treats that control as a first-class subject in the named book.

- **Titles** are the official NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 short control titles, which
  occasionally differ from a book's prose wording.
- **Volume VI (Implementation)** rows record where a control is *operationalized as
  deployable code*; the architecture book that closes the same control appears on
  the same row, so both the "what" and the "how" are visible at a glance.
- **Volume V (Training & Certification)** contributes only the controls whose own
  subject is the training program itself (AT-2 / AT-3), not the many controls it
  teaches.
- **Volumes VII–IX (ServiceNow coordination, multi-cloud DDI, and day-2
  operations)** record where a control is *coordinated, evidenced, or operated* —
  drift raised as a tracked ServiceNow task, a change gated by an approved record,
  an asset reconciled to the CM-8 join key. With one exception (**CM-5**, new in
  Vol VIII), these volumes re-close control numbers the architecture volumes
  already own, at a different plane (workflow/enforcement) — so a row here for one
  of these volumes means "this is where the control is *made operational and
  evidenced*," not a second independent closure claim. Actuation stays
  platform-native throughout.
- **Relationship to the compliance spine:** `aan-compliance-spine.yml` is the
  single source of truth for the machine-checked closures, and the per-book
  authorities tables are rendered from it and CI-gated against drift. The spine is
  being progressively back-filled book by book (~17 of 67 books carry closure rows
  today). A **machine-derived slice of this crosswalk is now rendered from the spine**
  by `render_crosswalk.py` into [`AAN_Spine_Crosswalk.md`](AAN_Spine_Crosswalk.md),
  behind the same drift gate as the per-book tables — so the spine-provable subset
  is auto-generated and cannot drift. **This master crosswalk remains
  hand-maintained** for the controls in books the spine has not yet back-filled, so
  it, not the generated slice, is presently the most complete series-wide control
  view, at the cost of being author-maintained for that remainder. The end state is
  for the generated slice to reach every book and this table to become fully
  spine-rendered.
- **Claim → evidence → test.** For the closure-bearing books, the spine now
  renders a generated, CI-gated [claim → evidence → test traceability
  matrix](AAN_Claim_Evidence_Test_Matrix.md): each of the 91 closure claims maps
  to its evidence slot, its implementing kit (where one exists), and the named
  falsifying test that would disprove it. It states the coverage honestly — the
  spine's generated closures cover **17 of 67 books**, and only **11 of 91**
  claims yet carry a named test — so a reader can see exactly which claims are
  verified, which are merely asserted, and which controls are hand-authored
  outside the spine.

::: {.aan-note}
"Addressed here" is a **coverage pointer, not a control-inheritance claim**. Whether
a control is fully inherited, partially satisfied, or shared depends on the boundary
and the assessor's determination — read the named book (and its evidence slot) for
the substantive treatment.
:::

# Master Control Crosswalk

Each NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control below is followed by the volume(s) and book(s) where the series addresses it. A control addressed in more than one book lists each — typically the architecture book that closes it, the Volume VI book that implements it as deployable code, and (for the coordination controls) the Volume VII/VIII/IX book that operates and evidences it through ServiceNow or the multi-cloud DDI plane. Control enhancements are listed as their own rows where a book cites the enhancement specifically.

The Volume VII/VIII/IX closures widen several themes: **KSI-CMT** gains CM-3
(change-controlled configuration), **KSI-CNA** gains the multi-cloud DDI naming
controls (SC-20, SC-22), **KSI-IAM** gains the identity/least-privilege and
credential-lifecycle controls the ServiceNow catalog governs (AC-2, AC-6, IA-5,
IA-5(2), SC-17, and the new CM-5 SoD gate), **KSI-MLA** gains the attestation and
telephony/DDI audit controls (CA-2, CA-5, AU-2), and **KSI-PIY** (asset
inventory / provenance) draws on the CM-8 join-key reconciliation and the CA-3
information-exchange mapping that run through Volumes VII, VIII, and IX.

# Notes and Caveats

- A control addressed in multiple books is intentional: the series separates
  architecture (closure) from implementation (Volume VI) and, in a few families,
  layers edge, host, and cloud-plane treatments across different books.
- Enhancement rows (e.g. AC-6(9)) appear separately only where a book cites the
  enhancement specifically; otherwise coverage is recorded at the base control.
- This index reflects the series as of the Date Code above. Regenerate it after any
  book's control tables change by re-running the extraction and merge, then
  re-rendering this appendix.

# Appendix — Controls Addressed but Not Yet Closed in the Spine
